action: press '1' -- choose English at the language prompt a fresh userdir opens on
commentary: English, the same as every form I ever filled in at the plant. Nothing here to think about.

action: press 'Up' -- move the cursor off Preset Character onto Custom Character
commentary: Not somebody else's. If I am going to write down honestly what I can and cannot do, I fill in every line of it myself.

action: press 'Return' -- open the custom creator; it asks first for the world
commentary: Right. Start at the top and work down, the way you fill in any form that matters.

action: press 'Return' -- open the world name field for editing
commentary: It wants a name for the place. The one it offered is somewhere in the middle of the country and this is not that.

action: press 'F' -- begin typing the name of the place over the one it suggested
commentary: Fern Creek. Two miles of it either side of the river, the mill at the north end, my rooms on the top floor of a two-family house.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: The creek is the first thing I would tell anybody about this town.

action: press 'r' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: It comes down out of the woods behind the high school.

action: press 'n' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: It goes under the road twice on its way through.

action: press 'space' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: And then into the river a quarter mile below the mill.

action: press 'C' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: My father fished it every April, when the water was still too cold to be pleasant about.

action: press 'r' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: He taught me to stand still and let the line do the work.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: That is the only thing he taught me that I have never once managed to apply anywhere else.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing the name of the place
commentary: Not today either. Today I want water I can drink, not water I can stand in.

action: press 'k' -- finish typing the name of the place
commentary: There. Where I am, written down, so the log starts with a place and not a feeling.

action: press 'Return' -- accept the name of the place
commentary: Accepted. I am not going to argue with the two settings underneath it either; they are what they are, and so is the week I have had.

action: press 'f' -- finish the world settings and move on to who I am
commentary: Finish. Now the part that actually matters, which is what I can do and what I cannot.

action: press 'Y' -- confirm the world settings; the map is generated from here
commentary: Yes. I am sure. Nothing on that page was going to be improved by me looking at it for another ten minutes.

action: press 'Down' -- move down off the shelter entry, looking for the one that is mine
commentary: Friends to the end. I had colleagues, and I sent them to the buses. There is a difference between those two words and I have had five days to think about it.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Hunted forever. No. Whatever is out there has not been following me. It has been standing where it was left.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: A helicopter crash. Nobody I have ever met has been in one of those.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Infected. I have looked at my arms twice an hour for five days and there is nothing on them.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Prison. The nearest one is forty miles south and I have never once been inside it.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Sheltered. That is the same roof as the first entry, with the door still shut and somebody else behind it.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Surrounded. Not yet. I have been careful and I have been lucky, and I know exactly which of the two has done more of the work.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Hunted again. Whoever wrote this list has a favourite.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: A burning building. I spent that whole afternoon making certain this would not be anybody's.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Bordered in. I would not have got out of the state on those roads that afternoon even if I had left at six with everybody else.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: A party. On a Tuesday, at my age, two miles from a live plant. No.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: A car crash. My truck is still in the lot at work with three quarters of a tank in it, because the road out was solid metal by four o'clock and I walked.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Hunted by the dead. Three entries on this page say the same thing in different words, and not one of them is what happened to me.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: A squatter. Not yet. Ask me again tonight, when I have to pick a room with a door.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: A large building. I have been in exactly one large building all week and it had a boiler house attached to it.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Low profile. That is a description of how I intend to spend today. It is not a description of how I got here.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list
commentary: Mass quarantine. There was no cordon on this side of the river. There was a list, a time, and a school car park.

action: press 'Down' -- keep reading down the list; the one below this is mine
commentary: A refugee centre. That is where the buses were going, and I have no idea at all whether they arrived.

action: press 'Down' -- land on the entry that is actually mine
commentary: Missed. There it is, one word, and it is the honest one. Not brave, not chosen, not unlucky. I was thirty feet from a drum gauge with two operators watching me when the last bus left the school.

action: press 'Return' -- take the missed-evacuation start
commentary: Take it. Stubbornness, it says, or ignorance, or bad luck. I will own the first one and argue about the other two another day.

action: press 'shift+Tab' -- step back to the first tab, to see how the accounting works before spending anything
commentary: Before I spend anything I want to see the ledger it is keeping. Twenty-two years of budgets taught me that much.

action: press 'Down' -- move off the entry that enforces no limits at all
commentary: The one it starts on says no limits are enforced. I have never in my life been handed a job with no limits enforced and I am not going to pretend today is that.

action: press 'Return' -- take the mode with three separate point pools, so every choice has to be paid for
commentary: Three separate budgets: what I am made of, what is wrong with me, and what I know how to do. Stat money can go downhill into the other two and never back up. That is a ledger I recognise.

action: press '@' -- correct the sex it assumed
commentary: It has me down as a man. I am not, and the rest of this form is going to be accurate whether or not that matters to anybody but me.

action: press '2' -- try the other key the form offers for the sex field
commentary: The first key I tried did nothing to it. Fine. There is always a second way in, and finding it is most of the job.

action: press 'n' -- open the field for the name, which is the one thing on this form I am certain of
commentary: Leave the sex field for a moment. The name I can do from memory.

action: press 'D' -- begin typing my name
commentary: Delphine. My grandmother's name. She came down from Quebec at fifteen to sew uppers in a shoe shop.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing my name
commentary: She never once in her life let anybody see her cry in a kitchen.

action: press 'l' -- continue typing my name
commentary: I have not managed that. I have managed most of the rest of it.

action: press 'p' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Everybody who ever paid me called me Del.

action: press 'h' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Two syllables was more than the floor of that mill ever had time for.

action: press 'i' -- continue typing my name
commentary: There is nobody left within twenty miles to shorten it now.

action: press 'n' -- continue typing my name
commentary: So it goes down in full.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Delphine.

action: press 'space' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Then the other half, which is my father's.

action: press 'O' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Ouellette. It is on the pension paperwork at the plant in his own handwriting.

action: press 'u' -- continue typing my name
commentary: He was a millwright in that building before the strike years.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing my name
commentary: He taught me to listen to a machine before I looked at it.

action: press 'l' -- continue typing my name
commentary: To keep my own tools clean.

action: press 'l' -- continue typing my name
commentary: And to fish the river in the spring, when the water is still too cold to be pleasant about it.

action: press 'e' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Two of those three are going to matter before dark.

action: press 't' -- continue typing my name
commentary: The tools are in a red steel box on a bench two miles from here.

action: press 't' -- continue typing my name
commentary: Which is the joke of my life, just at the minute.

action: press 'e' -- finish typing my name
commentary: There. All of it, spelled the way she spelled it.

action: press 'Return' -- accept the name
commentary: Accepted. Delphine Ouellette, forty-seven years old, of Mount Chase, Maine, and this is the fifth morning.

action: press 'question' -- ask the form which key does what, since two of my guesses did nothing
commentary: Stop guessing and read the instructions. That is not humility, it is just faster.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the key list; I have what I needed off it
commentary: There it is in black and white. The sex field wants the at sign, and the key I thought was doing nothing was moving the cursor down the list instead. Noted. Close it.

action: press 'shift+2' -- hold shift and strike the two, which is the at sign, for the sex field
commentary: Now the field itself. I am a woman of forty-seven and the form is going to say so before I put my name on the bottom of it.

action: press 'shift+4' -- set the clothing to the women's cut of the same working kit
commentary: And the clothes to match, since the boots and the shirt are mine and not borrowed off a shelf.

action: press 'a' -- open the age field
commentary: Age next. There is no point being coy about it: the number is half the reason my back is the way it is.

action: press '4' -- start typing my age over the number it guessed
commentary: It has guessed me twenty-four, which is generous and useless. Forty-seven.

action: press '7' -- finish typing my age
commentary: Forty-seven. Twenty-two of them in the same building, and I would not give those back.

action: press 'Return' -- accept my age
commentary: Accepted.

action: press 'Tab' -- move forward off the ledger tab
commentary: Forty-seven, and the field took it without comment. On to the work.

action: press 'Tab' -- move forward again, to the trade
commentary: Past the start I already chose. What I did for a living is the next line and it is the one I can answer without thinking.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter rather than scroll through every trade there is
commentary: The list of what people did for a living is a mile long and I already know my line on it. Search for it instead.

action: press 'M' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Mechanical.

action: press 'e' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Not electrical, not chemical, not the software people on the second floor.

action: press 'c' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Pumps, fans, gearboxes, bearings, headers, valves.

action: press 'h' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Anything that turns, anything under pressure, anything that gets hot.

action: press 'a' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Twenty-two years of it in one building.

action: press 'n' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: And the whole steam side of that building was mine by the end.

action: press 'i' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Not because I asked for it. Because everyone else who understood it left.

action: press 'c' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: Which is how you become the one they phone at three in the morning.

action: press 'a' -- type the trade I want to find
commentary: I never once let it ring out.

action: press 'l' -- finish typing the trade
commentary: Mechanical. There.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Show me what is left.

action: press 'Return' -- take the trade: mechanical engineer, two points
commentary: One entry left and it is mine. Mechanical engineer, and it costs me two out of the skills budget, which is the cheapest honest thing on this whole form.

action: press 'Tab' -- move forward past the background tab for now
commentary: There is a tab for what I did with my evenings. It can wait; the body comes first.

action: press 'Tab' -- move forward to the four numbers that describe the body
commentary: Four numbers for what I am made of. Thirty-eight points to spend on them and no way to get any of it back afterwards.

action: press 'plus' -- put a point into strength
commentary: Strength first. I have swung a two-foot pipe wrench at a seized coupling more mornings than I can count.

action: press 'plus' -- put a second point into strength
commentary: Ten. Above average, it says, and that is right: strong for a woman my age and no use pretending further.

action: press 'Down' -- move to the next number
commentary: That is what I can lift. What I cannot do with it comes later on the trait page.

action: press 'minus' -- take a point back out of dexterity
commentary: And here is where I pay for it. I have never been quick. I plan instead, and when a plan runs out I am the wrong woman to be standing there.

action: press 'Down' -- move to the next number
commentary: Seven. Below average, and I would rather the form said so than flattered me.

action: press 'plus' -- put a point into intelligence
commentary: This is the one I am actually good at.

action: press 'plus' -- put a second point into intelligence
commentary: Give me a machine and I will tell you what is wrong with it, usually before the cover is off.

action: press 'plus' -- put a third point into intelligence
commentary: That is not a boast. It is twenty-two years of being the one who had to know.

action: press 'plus' -- put a fourth point into intelligence
commentary: Twelve. Top tenth, it reckons. A head full of machines, which is all I have brought with me.

action: press 'Down' -- move to the last number
commentary: One point left over and one line to spend it on.

action: press 'plus' -- put the last point into perception
commentary: My eyes still read a gauge from across a bay and my ears are the best thing I own. Both of those live on this line.

action: press 'Tab' -- move forward to the traits, where the other side of the ledger lives
commentary: Ten, seven, twelve, nine, and nothing left over. Now the part I would rather write down myself than be surprised by later.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter on the trait list
commentary: Liabilities first. Nothing on the good side of this page is affordable until I have owned up to the bad.

action: press 'B' -- type the first liability
commentary: The back.

action: press 'a' -- type the first liability
commentary: Six years ago, on a lift I should have refused and did not.

action: press 'd' -- type the first liability
commentary: One end of a gearbox casing, a man off sick, and a shift that was already late.

action: press 'space' -- type the first liability
commentary: I felt it go and I finished the job anyway, which is the whole of my personality in one afternoon.

action: press 'B' -- finish typing the first liability
commentary: It has never once been right since.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the bad back, which earns three points back
commentary: Bad back. Thirty-five per cent off what I can carry, and it pays me three points for the privilege of being honest about it. I can still lift. I cannot carry. That is going to decide what I pick up and what I walk away from, all day.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter again for the second liability
commentary: Next. The sleep.

action: press 'I' -- type the second liability
commentary: Not since the winter my mother was dying and I lived in a chair beside her for four months.

action: press 'n' -- type the second liability
commentary: Two hours a night. Two more if I am owed a favour.

action: press 's' -- type the second liability
commentary: Other people lie down and go under like a thrown switch.

action: press 'o' -- type the second liability
commentary: I lie there and listen to the building and wait to be tired enough to be allowed in.

action: press 'm' -- finish typing the second liability
commentary: Tonight, whenever tonight comes, that is going to matter more than anything else on this page.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the insomnia, which earns two points back
commentary: Insomniac. A hard time falling asleep even under the best circumstances, it says, and it hands me two points for saying so out loud.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the third liability
commentary: One more. The legs.

action: press 'S' -- type the third liability
commentary: Slow. I have never been quick and I am slower now than I was at forty.

action: press 'l' -- type the third liability
commentary: Fifteen per cent off my pace on flat ground, and there is nothing flat about a street with cars across it.

action: press 'o' -- type the third liability
commentary: Running is not a plan available to me. It has not been for years.

action: press 'w' -- type the third liability
commentary: So every room I go into, I want to know the way out of before I am in it.

action: press 'space' -- type the third liability
commentary: That is not caution. That is arithmetic.

action: press 'F' -- finish typing the third liability
commentary: Three liabilities, eight points, and every one of them true.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the slow feet, which earns three points back
commentary: Slow footed. Three points back, and the plain truth of what my legs are worth on a street I have to leave in a hurry.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the first thing I am actually good for
commentary: Eight points in the pot, all of it borrowed against my own body. Now what it bought.

action: press 'G' -- type the first boon
commentary: The ears.

action: press 'o' -- type the first boon
commentary: I can hear a bad bearing through a concrete floor.

action: press 'o' -- type the first boon
commentary: That is not a party trick, it is the whole of preventive maintenance.

action: press 'd' -- type the first boon
commentary: And in five days I have learned it works on rooms as well as on gearboxes.

action: press 'space' -- type the first boon
commentary: I can hear which ones have something in them long before there is anything to see.

action: press 'H' -- finish typing the first boon
commentary: It has kept me alive twice already and I did not have to be brave either time.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the good hearing for one point
commentary: Good hearing, one point. Cheapest thing on the page and the most useful thing I own.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the second boon
commentary: And one more.

action: press 'F' -- type the second boon
commentary: The hands.

action: press 'a' -- type the second boon
commentary: Twenty-two years of threading nuts into holes I could not see.

action: press 's' -- type the second boon
commentary: They come back from a slip before my head has caught up.

action: press 't' -- type the second boon
commentary: Cuts close, knuckles heal, and I have never once needed stitches from that building.

action: press 'space' -- type the second boon
commentary: It is the one part of me that has not aged at the rate the rest has.

action: press 'H' -- finish typing the second boon
commentary: Two points, and worth it: I am going to be handling broken glass and torn metal all day.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the fast healing for two points
commentary: Fast healer, two points. Five liabilities and boons between them, three points spent against eight earned, and I am five to the good with the skills page still to pay for.

action: press 'shift+Tab' -- go back a tab
commentary: Five points left over from being honest about myself. Now what I did with my evenings.

action: press 'shift+Tab' -- go back again, to the background
commentary: Because a working life is not the only place a person learns anything.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter on the background list
commentary: The honest one first, again.

action: press 'N' -- type the habit I have and cannot put down
commentary: There is nothing in my shirt pocket but the pocket.

action: press 'i' -- type the habit
commentary: I quit twice in my thirties and failed twice.

action: press 'c' -- type the habit
commentary: One hour without and I am mean. Two and I cannot hold a thought in a straight line.

action: press 'o' -- type the habit
commentary: I know precisely how the rest of that goes, and there is no shop between here and the river that has not already been emptied.

action: press 't' -- finish typing the habit
commentary: So it is going to be a hard day, and none of it will be the day's fault.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the nicotine dependence, which earns a point back
commentary: Nicotine dependence. It earns me a point, which is the only good thing the habit has ever done for me.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the first aid
commentary: Now the useful evenings.

action: press 'F' -- type the first useful thing
commentary: The mill sent us to the first-aid refresher every spring.

action: press 'i' -- type the first useful thing
commentary: Most people slept through it. I paid attention every single year.

action: press 'r' -- type the first useful thing
commentary: Because a man went into a nip point on the third floor in ninety-nine and nobody on that shift knew what to do with him.

action: press 's' -- type the first useful thing
commentary: I can stop a bleed, splint a wrist, and tell the difference between a wound that is frightening and one that is killing you.

action: press 't' -- finish typing the first useful thing
commentary: Today that is worth more than anything else I know.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the first aid for one point
commentary: First aid, one point. I would pay five.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the river
commentary: And the river.

action: press 'F' -- type the second useful thing
commentary: My father taught me to fish it in April.

action: press 'i' -- type the second useful thing
commentary: Which sounds like sentiment and is not: it is how you find water and read weather coming up a valley.

action: press 's' -- type the second useful thing
commentary: And how you learn not to eat something stupid because it looked all right.

action: press 'h' -- finish typing the second useful thing
commentary: There is a creek in this town and I am going to need it before the day is out.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the fishing for one point
commentary: Fishing, one point, and the outdoorsman that comes free with it. Being wet is going to be part of today.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the bench work
commentary: One more that is really just the day job spilling over.

action: press 'M' -- type the third useful thing
commentary: Machinist.

action: press 'a' -- type the third useful thing
commentary: Half the work in an old plant is that the part you want is not in the crib.

action: press 'c' -- type the third useful thing
commentary: So you build one out of whatever is on the bench.

action: press 'h' -- type the third useful thing
commentary: A bracket, a wedge, a handle, a length of stock jammed across the inside of a window.

action: press 'i' -- finish typing the third useful thing
commentary: That last one I am going to want tonight.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the beginner machinist for two points
commentary: Machinist, beginner, two points. Fabrication and a bit more mechanics on top of what the job already gave me.

action: press 'slash' -- open the filter for the licence
commentary: And the last one, which is only on here because it is true.

action: press 'D' -- type the last background
commentary: I drive. Or I did.

action: press 'r' -- type the last background
commentary: Down through a dead town at three in the morning more times than I can count, with the heater going and nobody on the road.

action: press 'i' -- type the last background
commentary: My truck is in the lot at work and I am not going to see it again.

action: press 'v' -- finish typing the last background
commentary: But if I find something with keys in it and a clear road, I can move it, and that costs nothing to write down.

action: press 'Return' -- apply the filter
commentary: Find it.

action: press 'Tab' -- leave the verified licence selected and move toward skills
commentary: The licence is already there. Leave it alone and keep going.

action: press 'Tab' -- cross the traits tab toward skills
commentary: The bad back, the sleeplessness, and the slow feet are all debts I already know.

action: press 'Tab' -- open the skills tab
commentary: Last, the things I can still do when somebody gets close enough that a tool is not enough.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the highlighted bashing skill increase
commentary: A hammer, a crowbar, a length of pipe—if I have to swing one, I need to know where the weight goes.

action: press 'Down' -- move from bashing toward melee
commentary: An edge can cut clean, but I have spent my life with blunt steel and handles.

action: press 'Down' -- move from cutting toward melee
commentary: Getting out of the way matters more than looking brave.

action: press 'Down' -- highlight melee
commentary: Any of it starts with footing, distance, and not freezing.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the verified two-level melee increase
commentary: Two hard lessons: keep my balance, and strike only when I mean it.

action: press 'Tab' -- open the summary after spending the final skill point
commentary: That is enough. I know what I know, and there is nothing left to pretend.

action: press 'Tab' -- advance from the verified summary to the finish confirmation
commentary: The numbers close. The life on the page is mine, debts and all. I am done choosing.

action: press 'Y' -- confirm the finished custom character and wait for the world to appear
commentary: Yes. This is me. Find a door that closes, find water, find one good wrench, and keep breathing.

action: press 'Escape' -- open the in-game main menu before the first move
commentary: Before I take a single step, I need one quiet breath and a clear beginning.

action: press 'e' -- invoke the verified Quicksave menu item without quitting
commentary: Restaurant. Eight in the morning. Too many dead to the west. I fix that in my head before I move.
